title: WPSB/351/2026 of DR TANU MITTAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SUBHASH UPADHYAY
18TH JUNE, 2026
WRIT PETITION (S/B) NO. 351 OF 2026
Dr. Tanu Mittal ......Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....Respondents.
Counsel for the Petitioner : Mr. Sagar Kothari, learned counsel.
Counsel for the State : Mr. B.P.S. Mer, learned Standing
Counsel.
JUDGMENT :(per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
1. The present writ petition has been filed assailing
the transfer order dated 09.06.2026, whereby the
petitioner, who is presently posted as Assistant Professor,
Sociology, Government P.G. College, New Tehri, has been
transferred in the same capacity to Government P.G.
College, Talwari, District Chamoli.
2. The case of the petitioner is that she has been
transferred on complaint without holding proper inquiry
and, therefore, it is in violation of Section 18(4) of the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017
(hereinafter referred to as "the Act").
3. On the other hand, learned State Counsel
submitted that the transfer was made in exercise of power
1

UKHC010104952026
2026:UHC:5041-DB
under Section 18(5) of the Act, which reads as under:-
"18(5) The competent authority may issue
positing/ transfer orders besides the transfer to be made
as per clause (1) to (4) aforesaid in separate and
different period also and it shall not be necessary to
bring such cases before the transfer committee:
Provided that on transfers made on administrative
grounds the competent authority shall have to take
approval from the one rank higher officer."
4. As the Department has sought to bring the
transfer within the purview of sub-section (5) of Section 18
of the Act, therefore, such transfer should have had the
approval of officer one rank higher than the competent
authority. Consequently, we required the Department to
place on record material to indicate that the approval from
the higher authority was obtained.
5. Learned State Counsel has obtained further
instructions and has place for our perusal the notings on
the official file, which indicate that the Department had
obtained approval of the concerned Minister for transfer of
the petitioner on administrative grounds.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner tried to
contend that the noting indicates that the transfer was
made on complaint. In other words, he has tried to bring
the case under sub-section (4) of Section 18, where enquiry
2

UKHC010104952026
2026:UHC:5041-DB
is needed if transfer is made on a complaint. However, the
record does not lead to any such conclusion, as in respect
of other employees, who had been transferred on
complaints, it was so mentioned specifically in the note-sheet. As against the name of the petitioner, it is not stated
that she was being transferred on basis of complaint. Thus,
we find no illegality in the impugned transfer order.
7. The writ petition lacks merit and is, accordingly,
dismissed.
8. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed
of.
MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.
SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.
Dated: 18th June, 2026
NISHANT
